Murske tiivistetään esimerkiksi yliajamalla. Urakoitsija vastaa päällystettävillä alueilla olevien kaivojen teleskooppi- ja muiden kansistojen sekä venttiilihattujen laskemisesta työn ajaksi sekä nostosta päällysteen tasoon. {"sourceType":"ESA Tender Action","sourceSystem":"ESA esa-star Publication","sourcePage":"https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int/ESATenderActions/filter/open","id":181257,"idEra":24487,"activityNumber":"1000045301","contractNumber":"","tanumber":"1-13225","title":"S2-SD-12 ROCKET BODY RE-ENTRY RISK FALCON 9 CASE STUDY - EXPRO+","description":"On February 19, 2025, at around 4:46 a.m. local time, over Polish territory, in the area west of the city of Poznan, an uncontrolled re-entry into the lower layers of Earth's atmosphere occurred involving a stage of the Falcon 9 upper stage. It was followed by the fragmentation of the object and the fall of its parts to the Earth's surface over an area spanning several dozen kilometres.Fortunately, re-entry events where fragments are identified on-ground are rare and when the associate risk does not materialise, they provide a scientific opportunity. Large uncertainties on destructive re-entry physics and dynamics in the very low Earth orbit ( < 150km ) can be constrained by studying the physics associated with the fragment generation and final impact location, as demonstrated by recent studies targeting break-ups recoded by on-ground all-sky telescope systems.The activity aims to maximize the scientific return of the Falcon 9 re-entry event, without usage of proprietary information.
